goal: make --update refuse to pin an uncommitted tree in the pinned scope

scenarios.what: one uncommitted packages/** source edit --update must refuse and leave the baseline byte-identical
scenarios.mutation: appended '// r2t2 dirty-tree probe' to packages/schematic/src/types.ts
scenarios.stdout: {"status":"UPDATE_REFUSED_DIRTY_TREE","reason":"uncommitted changes inside the pinned scope; the baseline was not written","files":[" M packages/schematic/src/types.ts"],"hint":"commit or revert these paths, then re-run --update; --force-dirty pins them anyway and prints a warning"}

scenarios.what: restore the probe edit, --check returns to FRESH
escape hatch writes despite a dirty tree, prints a banner, and really pins the dirty bytes
scenarios.stderr: !!!! WARNING: --force-dirty is pinning an UNCOMMITTED tree. / !! The baseline will certify bytes that are in no commit. / !!    M packages/schematic/src/types.ts

afterRestoreCheck.why: proof the escape hatch pinned the uncommitted bytes: restoring the file makes the tree differ from what was pinned

existingScripts.verdict: PASS 21 comps / 8 part / 13 netflag / 55 wires / 2 pages

notes: The guard reuses the same notion of 'pinned' as snapshot(): packages/**, root configs, every tsconfig*.json. docs/** dirt does not block, which is deliberate: evidence files are not hashed into the baseline.
--force-dirty is the only override and it prints a four-line banner plus forcedDirty:true in the JSON, so a forced pin is visible in the artifact forever.
A git failure refuses with UPDATE_REFUSED_GIT_UNAVAILABLE (cannot prove clean is not clean).
Pre-existing quirk not touched: --update always writes BASELINE_PATH even when --baseline <path> is passed; --check honours --baseline. Out of scope for this task.
